best_for: Windows users who need to turn an ISO into a bootable USB stick, for example to reinstall Windows 11 on a PC Microsoft says is unsupported or to try a Linux distro.
description:
Rufus is a free tool that formats USB flash drives and makes them bootable. Pete Batard writes it, and the program is signed by his company, Akeo Consulting. It is GPLv3, built from public source, and translated by volunteers into dozens of languages.

Use it to make an install stick from an ISO for Windows or for Linux systems such as Debian, Fedora or Kali, or for rescue tools like Clonezilla, GParted and Hiren's Boot CD. It also helps when a PC has no system installed at all, or when you need to boot DOS to flash a BIOS or other firmware. On a DOS drive, Rufus picks a keyboard layout to match your system's locale.

points.title: No install, about 2 MB
points.text: Rufus is a single executable you download and run. The project lists Windows 8 or later as the requirement and offers builds for x86, x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Windows 11 on older PCs
points.text: After you press Start, a dialog offers to remove setup checks such as TPM, Secure Boot and the online Microsoft account. Rufus uses switches Microsoft built into setup rather than patching files, so a future Windows release can remove them. It cannot get around the CPU features Windows 11 24H2 needs.

points.title: It can fetch the ISO for you
points.text: A Download button pulls Windows ISOs straight from Microsoft's servers. It only appears when update checks are on and Rufus could reach its signed download script at launch.

points.title: One image per drive
points.text: Rufus writes one bootable image to a stick. The FAQ says multiboot drives are out of scope and points to tools like Ventoy instead. Linux images can get a persistent partition, except in DD mode.

points.title: Windows To Go, with care
points.text: Rufus can build a Windows that runs from USB, but only when Rufus runs on Windows 8 or later, on the same Windows version as the image or newer. Slow drives make it painful; the FAQ says a job over 20 minutes means the stick is not fit for it.

points.title: It goes online
points.text: Update checks are on by default when the file is named rufus.exe, and Rufus also downloads boot files and UEFI revocation lists as needed. Settings are written to the registry even for the portable build.

points.title: Windows only
points.text: There is no Mac or Linux version and the author has no plans for one. The listing here keeps 26 versions.
